subject: Draft MSA — forum selection & equitable relief clause (Monsoon Labs)
content:
From: Sara Albright <sara@monsoonlabs.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Jean-Paul Grenier <jp@monsoonlabs.com>, Monsoon Labs Legal <legal@monsoonlabs.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Draft MSA redlines — forum selection and provisional remedies

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks again for the productive negotiation yesterday. Attached is our redline of the Master Services Agreement focused on the legal block items — choice of law, dispute resolution, and the section on provisional remedies / equitable relief.

High-level summary:
- We propose English law, with arbitration in London (LCIA) for disputes, to align with our EU operations and investor expectations.
- We are happy to accept an injunctive relief carveout (i.e., parties can seek provisional measures in courts) but request the seat remain London and that any interim measures be pursued in English courts.
- For emergency relief (ex parte injunctive relief), we want a clear process: notice to be provided by us and a 7-day preservation hold on data while a seat decision is made.

Please see the attached redline and a short comment matrix explaining our rationale for each change. We are trying to avoid a broad consent-to-jurisdiction clause that would expose us to multiple forum obligations.

Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood can: (1) accept English law and LCIA seat; (2) agree to our proposed 7-day preservation hold for emergency measures; and (3) provide a limited carveout for injunctive relief in English courts only?

We'd like to close legal terms by 12/08 so we can get the order form signed by 12/15.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Albright
Head of Legal Ops, Monsoon Labs
[Attachment: Monsoon_MSA_redlines_v1.pdf (redline)]
[Attachment: Monsoon_MSA_comment_matrix.xlsx]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sara Albright <sara@monsoonlabs.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2027 11:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — forum selection and provisional remedies

Sara — thanks for the redline and the matrix. Appreciate the clarity. Looping in Karthik and Aditya from our contracts & legal team.

Quick flags from Redwood's side:
- Redwood's standard is California law (State of California) with courts in San Francisco for non-arbitral relief. We generally accept arbitration seats outside CA only where there are strong commercial reasons and reciprocal enforcement assurances.
- We are open to an equitable relief carveout, but we need it to be neutral and reciprocal — e.g., either party can seek provisional remedies in a local court where relief is expedient, not restricted to English courts.
- The 7-day data preservation hold is reasonable operationally, but we need clarity on scope (what systems, logs, KV cache retention, and who bears the cost).

Action items:
1) Karthik / Aditya — please see the redline and advise on whether a compromise on seat (e.g., arbitration with seat in London but choice of law in California) is workable given Redwood precedent.
2) Sara — if Monsoon can accept a neutral interim measures clause (either party may seek provisional relief in a local court to preserve rights), we can propose language tying injunctive relief to an agreed notice and short good-faith coordination window.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Albright <sara@monsoonlabs.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2027 08:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — forum selection and provisional remedies

Sara — quick response from legal counsel:
- We generally prefer single-jurisdiction choice of law and forum to avoid parallel proceedings. Typical Redwood compromise has been: choice of law = State of California; arbitration = AAA/ICC with seat mutually agreed (often New York or neutral seat) — but we can be flexible for strategic customers.
- We can accept LCIA seat in London if Monsoon agrees to California substantive law (i.e., governing law) and a limited injunctive relief carveout that allows local interim measures. The rationale is Redwood wants to preserve sensible predictability of substantive law while allowing efficient provisional remedies locally.
- Draft language proposal (high level): either party may seek provisional or interim relief in any competent court to preserve its rights pending constitution of the tribunal. Such relief shall not be deemed a waiver of the agreement to arbitrate.

Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

-----
From: Jean-Paul Grenier <jp@monsoonlabs.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>, Sara Albright <sara@monsoonlabs.com>
Date: Mon, 29 Nov 2027 14:20:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — forum selection and provisional remedies

Thanks Karthik — appreciate the suggested compromise. A couple of follow-ups from our side:
- Monsoon's business stakeholders and compliance team are firm on English governing law for historic reasons with our investors. Switching governing law to California would require additional board approvals and introduce delay.
- If Redwood is insistent on California law, could we consider a split approach: (1) governing law = English law for sections relating to data/privacy/security, (2) California law for commercial sections (fees, termination)? We know split-law approaches are unusual but may be a pragmatic workaround.
- On provisional relief: the language Karthik proposes looks good provided the carveout explicitly allows emergency search-and-seizure style relief (where applicable) and sets a preservation hold timeline (7 days) for Redwood to coordinate.

JP
General Counsel, Monsoon Labs
[Attachment: Monsoon_counterproposals.docx]

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jean-Paul Grenier <jp@monsoonlabs.com>, Sara Albright <sara@monsoonlabs.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Dec 2027 15:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Draft MSA redlines — forum selection and provisional remedies

JP / Sara — thanks for the transparency. We want to keep this moving and avoid board-level friction on both sides. Proposed path forward from Redwood: 

1) Governing law: agree to a limited split-law approach narrowly scoped to data/privacy/security provisions governed by English law; all commercial terms (fees, payment, limitation of liability, indemnities) to remain governed by California law. This split applies only where absolutely necessary and shall be explicitly flagged in the SOW/Order Form.

2) Arbitration / seat: accept LCIA as the arbitral seat if Monsoon accepts California substantive law for commercial sections as above. Tribunal procedural rules remain LCIA.

3) Provisional remedies / injunctive relief: adopt Karthik's drafting with clarifying operational language:
   - Either party may seek provisional or interim relief in any competent court to preserve rights pending constitution of the tribunal; such relief will not be deemed a waiver of the agreement to arbitrate.
   - Where the seeking party requests data preservation or cache retention, Redwood will implement a preservation hold for up to 7 calendar days and will notify Monsoon's legal contact with scope and estimated incremental costs. Any extraordinary costs associated with extended preservation (>7 days) will be discussed in good faith.

4) Execution timeline: if Monsoon agrees to the above, Redwood will produce a redline within 48 hours and Laura will coordinate the final Order Form for signature.

Please confirm by EOD Friday 2027-12-03 if the path above is acceptable, otherwise flag the specific point(s) requiring escalation.

Best,
Evelyn Hart
Head of Commercial Legal, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_response_draft.docx]
